errors.text: The hypothesis assigns the critical ordering evolution to the B2 phase, whereas the target mechanism is enhanced L12 ordering in FCC domains approaching Ni3Al stoichiometry.
It substitutes a semi-coherent/incoherent boundary transition for the target evolution of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries and stress concentration at jagged boundary tips.
It omits the target dislocation mechanism: increased antiphase-boundary energy and elastic modulus suppress cross-slip and promote planar slip in ordered FCC domains.

The proposed high-temperature recovery through B2 coarsening, Orowan bypass, or incoherency does not reconstruct the target recovery through reduced L12 ordering and ductile transition-zone formation along phase boundaries.
It does not provide the required specific temperature boundary of approximately below 550°C, 550–750°C, and above 750°C; the invented order and misfit thresholds are unsupported.
